publicComments.name: Jenny and Archer
publicComments.summary: Two Orion students expressed concern about the proposed 3rd/4th grade combo class, arguing it would result in unequal instruction and asking for two dedicated 3rd grade classes.

publicComments.name: Allison Rhodes
publicComments.summary: Representing Clifford Elementary teachers, she presented a petition outlining concerns about multiple combination classrooms, lack of instructional aide support, impact on student achievement, and disproportionate numbers of IEP/504 students, requesting elimination of combo classes.

publicComments.name: Andrew Chan
publicComments.summary: Parent of four future Orion students, praised the Mandarin Immersion program and argued that a 3rd/4th combo class would dilute the critical 3rd grade immersion experience, proposing instead to recruit enough students to justify two full 3rd grade classes.

publicComments.name: Richard Palm
publicComments.summary: Parent of two Orion MI students shared his daughters' positive experiences in the program and expressed concern that a combo class would harm his younger daughter who needs hands-on attention.

publicComments.name: Jason Madsen
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of many 2nd grade MI families, he described the proposed combo class structure, expressed concern about reduced Mandarin instructional consistency and quality for students with IEPs/504s, and asked the district to provide two dedicated 3rd grade classes.

publicComments.name: Ann Law
publicComments.summary: Twin mother in the Orion MI program asked the district to reconsider the combo class proposal as it would force her to choose which twin gets the combo class experience versus a standard one.

publicComments.name: Julia Redesnerda
publicComments.summary: Parent of a rising 3rd grader and incoming TK student in the MI program advocated for two fully funded, fully staffed 3rd grade classrooms, warning that the combo proposal could discourage families from staying in the program.

publicComments.name: Heidi Glasser
publicComments.summary: Long-time MI program parent who recalled the program's growth since the 2015 pilot year urged the board to invest in the program's sustainability so parents don't face the difficult choice between MI and North Star Academy.

publicComments.name: Jasper Chen
publicComments.summary: Parent of an Orion 2nd grader and TK student praised Principal Winnie's leadership and echoed the call to build the enrollment pipeline rather than create compromises that might cause parents to leave the MI program.

publicComments.name: Aida Vázquez
publicComments.summary: Spoke in Spanish (with board translation) as a Garfield School parent to oppose proposed changes to bilingual programs, arguing that the current bilingual program has been effective for her children and many families and should be strengthened rather than changed.

publicComments.name: Michelle Strode
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of incoming TK parents at Orion's Mandarin Immersion Program, requested expansion of after-school programs (Play Thrive) to accommodate working families whose TK placement is not viable without reliable after-school care.

publicComments.name: Sally Dunaway Young
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for expanding the Mandarin Immersion TK program but urged allocation of additional campus space so that aftercare providers can expand to serve working families whose children cannot participate without afternoon coverage.

publicComments.name: May Liang
publicComments.summary: Advocated for the expansion of Play Thrive after-school program at Orion, sharing that her daughter secured a kindergarten spot but the family was waitlisted for after-school care, and requested a third classroom be added.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: As a parent whose child attended Mandarin Immersion and now attends North Star Academy, thanked Superintendent Baker for his long-standing support of both programs.

publicComments.name: Josh Hill
publicComments.summary: Echoed other parents' excitement about the Orion Mandarin program acceptance for his child while expressing anxiety about after-school care availability and requesting program expansion.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez-Monet
publicComments.summary: As a longtime Hoover community volunteer and parent, advocated for smaller class sizes, noting that the single Spanish kindergarten class at Hoover has grown too large and students with varied needs are not receiving adequate individual attention.

publicComments.name: Sophia Santos
publicComments.summary: As a first grade teacher at Hoover with 27 students including high proportions of IEP, multilingual, and behavioral-needs students, urged the board to prioritize manageable class sizes citing research showing smaller class sizes improve academic and social outcomes.

publicComments.name: Kristy Herrera
publicComments.summary: As a Hoover kindergarten teacher with deep personal roots in RCSD as a former student, parent, and 34-year educator, passionately urged the board to invest in smaller class sizes and equitable distribution of students across the district, arguing the current system is neither equal nor equitable.

publicComments.name: Kristi Herrera
publicComments.summary: Kindergarten teacher at Hoover with 24 years of experience described challenges of large class sizes and high proportions of students with IEPs, multilingual learners, and behavioral needs, urging the board to create classrooms structured for learning.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: Retired Redwood City kindergarten teacher advocated for smaller class sizes and faster timelines for identifying and assessing students with special needs.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: Music teacher and RCTA Membership Chair announced that the Redwood City Teachers Association unanimously voted to endorse the Redwood City School District parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Thomas Rogerson
publicComments.summary: Parent of children at Henry Ford and North Star argued that teacher quality matters most to student achievement, urged the board to consider equity and teacher retention when evaluating class sizes, and noted that heterogeneous classrooms deserve more targeted support.

publicComments.name: Aracely Flores Mendoza
publicComments.summary: Second-year education specialist at Hoover described unsustainable caseloads for resource teachers and requested that the board provide two aides for resource teachers at Hoover for the next school year.

publicComments.name: Ann Briljafa
publicComments.summary: Retired teacher shared data about TK students' IEPs, SSTs, and behavioral challenges arriving in next year's kindergarten, arguing that small class sizes in kindergarten are essential to early literacy outcomes.

publicComments.name: Lisbeth Estrada and Jesus Ponce
publicComments.summary: Hoover parents (speaking in Spanish with English translation) thanked the district for investments at Hoover and requested extended TK hours, expansion of TK, and instructional assistants in kindergarten and first grade to support personalized learning.

publicComments.name: Heather McCormick
publicComments.summary: Henry Ford parent and classroom volunteer described how a class of 32 third graders limits space for curriculum activities and leaves some students without adequate attention.

publicComments.name: Augustine Espino
publicComments.summary: Parent and community advocate expressed concern about large class sizes, reported that he has been spreading awareness of the parcel tax among parents, and urged accountability to the Latino community if the tax passes.

publicComments.name: Pam Barash
publicComments.summary: 36-year kindergarten teacher at Henry Ford described how student needs have grown dramatically over her career and urged the board not to allow kindergarten class sizes to reach 30-to-1, warning that joyful personalized learning is impossible at that ratio.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez-Monet
publicComments.summary: Hoover parent since 2017 described firsthand observations of the impact of having only one Spanish kindergarten class and asked the board to reduce class sizes and restore a second Spanish kindergarten section.

publicComments.name: Patricia Renderos
publicComments.summary: Parent (speaking in Spanish) expressed excitement about TK results, said she is encouraging other families to enroll in TK, and thanked the board and teachers for their work.

publicComments.name: Sophia Santos
publicComments.summary: First-grade teacher at Hoover in her first year with the district shared that managing 27 students with varied needs is overwhelming and urged the board to take steps to reduce class sizes.

publicComments.name: Jackie Moore
publicComments.summary: Special education teacher and Hoover parent advocated for paraeducators in every K-2 classroom, smaller class sizes, a hard cap on SLC caseloads, and a para for each RLC teacher.

publicComments.name: Rajanesh Patarath
publicComments.summary: Marine Corps veteran and father of a kindergarten student in Ms. Herrera's class praised her teaching and asked the board to consider the impact of increasing class sizes on students' ability to receive individualized attention.

items.title: Labor Association Comments

publicComments.name: Brenna Gear
publicComments.summary: RCTA President asked the board to officially endorse the Prop 55 extension and announced that over upcoming board meetings teachers will speak on negotiation topics including class size, salary, and safety.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker (CSEA/classified representative)
publicComments.summary: Classified employees' representative argued that classified staff consistently receive less equitable compensation than teachers and administrators and called on the board to provide fair and equitable salary increases that reflect the real cost of living.

publicComments.name: Steve (Orion PTO Mandarin Immersion Co-Op)
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of the Orion PTO, he thanked the board for prior feedback, noted Orion sustained deep cuts last year, and advocated for retaining the bilingual guest teacher given the school's unique dual-program needs.

publicComments.name: Patricia Renderos (interpreter for Hoover parent)
publicComments.summary: Interpreted a Hoover parent's comments requesting coaching cycles, free planning time, and professional development with modeling to support and retain teachers, especially for TK and elementary students.

publicComments.name: Agustin Espino
publicComments.summary: Asked the board to maintain mental health programs and TK programs, and urged equitable decision-making for the Latino community when making cuts, noting the achievement gap between Hoover and other schools.

publicComments.name: Lizbeth Estrada (interpreted by Patricia Renderos)
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent with children in 2nd and 3rd grade, she advocated strongly against cutting reading and math specialists, warning that reduced MTSS tier 2/3 supports would cost more in the long run and urging the board to protect intervention specialist positions and professional development funding.

publicComments.name: Cristian Vasquez (interpreted by Patricia Renderos)
publicComments.summary: A Clifford parent who shared his personal testimony about how current school resources and specialists have greatly benefited his son compared to the limited resources his older daughter had, and expressed concern about cuts to staff and specialists.

publicComments.name: Tina Yim
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent highlighted that RCMIS fundraising pressure has increased 30% to 410,000 for 2026-27, advocated for retaining Orion's bilingual guest teacher, and requested continued district investment in the Mandarin Immersion program through Kennedy Middle School.

publicComments.name: Araceli Flores Mendoza
publicComments.summary: A Resource Learning Center teacher and Hoover alumna advocated for more resources, staffing, and support for special education students, noting the three RLC teachers are spread thin with minimal aide support.

publicComments.name: Lisa Onofre (interpreted by Patricia Renderos)
publicComments.summary: A Clifford parent urged the board not to cut food services or cafeteria staff, to prioritize math education to address declining scores, and warned against selling district property to private interests.

publicComments.name: Tina Mercer
publicComments.summary: Roosevelt principal advocated for retaining admin IEP sub coverage for TK-5 schools without assistant principals, citing approximately 150 IEP meetings per year at Roosevelt and noting that without coverage, she would lose roughly 250 hours annually from classroom and staff support.

publicComments.name: Laura Ramirez (interpreted by Patricia Renderos)
publicComments.summary: An Adelante Selby Spanish immersion parent expressed understanding of the budget necessity but urged the board to protect resources that directly impact student learning, safety, and wellness, and to continue supporting family engagement organizations like Familias Unidas.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent shared how school counseling helped her son with post-pandemic anxiety and urged the board to protect mental health and counseling resources as essential for student success.

publicComments.name: Rita Melton
publicComments.summary: A fourth grade teacher at Adelante Selby advocated for retaining mental health professionals, MTSS TOSAs, and guest teachers, warning that cuts to these positions would increase pressure on principals and teachers and hurt student achievement.

publicComments.name: Dora Ramirez (interpreted by Patricia Renderos)
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent with children in 2nd and 8th grade (special education) urged the board not to cut music or STEAM programs, requested more special ed classroom options for middle school grades 6-8, and asked that no cuts be made that would negatively impact students.

publicComments.name: Finbar Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A third-grade Orion student described his passion for learning advanced topics like paleoanthropology and asked the district to offer more challenging coursework because he struggles with boredom and distraction due to his disability.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Advocated for policy changes to support academic acceleration for high-ability students, citing research, equity concerns, and asking the board to reconsider Board Policy 5123 and reinstate honors courses at Kennedy Middle School.

publicComments.name: Saoirse (Usha)
publicComments.summary: An Orion student heading to Kennedy next year described her own learning journey, her 97th-percentile 8th-grade iReady score, and urged the board to make advanced coursework available at Kennedy Middle School.

publicComments.name: Elmer Molina
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent (comments translated) asked the board to make air conditioning a top priority at KIPP Excelencia because students are suffering from the heat.

publicComments.name: Jose Talavera
publicComments.summary: Associate Director of Advocacy for KIPP urged the board to include KIPP Excelencia campus upgrades—especially air conditioning—in the upcoming Facilities Master Plan retreat, and invited trustees to a community tree-planting event on Monday.

publicComments.name: Carmen Flores
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent (comments translated) asked the board to include KIPP Excelencia in the facilities budget, citing heat and water quality concerns affecting students.

publicComments.name: Juan Bale
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent (comments translated) congratulated Hoover on its improvements and urged the board to extend similar facility upgrades—including the playground area—to KIPP Excelencia.

publicComments.name: Chris Terry
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent praised the district's equity programs but argued that without advanced coursework at Kennedy, well-resourced families resort to expensive private tutoring, creating inequity, and asked the board to offer advanced classes at the middle school level.

publicComments.name: Pam Barish
publicComments.summary: A 34-year kindergarten teacher at Henry Ford raised concerns about the disruptive and impractical portable air conditioning units installed over spring break and also flagged the elimination of minimum days at the start of next school year that had previously allowed kindergarten teachers to assess new students.

publicComments.name: May
publicComments.summary: A professional mathematician and Orion parent advocated for increased access to advanced middle school curriculum, arguing it is an equity issue that ensures high-ability students from all socioeconomic backgrounds receive the preparation they need.

publicComments.name: Azil
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student at Orion Mandarin Immersion advocated for an advanced ELA class at Kennedy Middle School, noting that English is her third language and advanced coursework would help her pursue her dream of becoming a pilot.

publicComments.name: Nia Seeberger
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student originally from China argued that students without English-speaking parents or outside resources especially need advanced ELA coursework at Kennedy to be prepared for AP classes in high school.

publicComments.name: Maple
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student scoring at the 92nd percentile nationally for 8th-grade ELA described feeling bored and disengaged in her current class and asked the board to add advanced ELA at Kennedy so she does not have to consider private school.

publicComments.name: Maya Rose Felix
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student with parents who could not assist with homework asked the board to add advanced English at Kennedy, saying it is critical to her goal of becoming a lawyer and succeeding in AP coursework in high school.

publicComments.name: Greta
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade Orion student who chose Kennedy over North Star to continue Mandarin study asked the board to add advanced English and other challenging classes at Kennedy, noting she loses focus when material is too slow.

publicComments.name: Luis Velazquez
publicComments.summary: A parent and executive coach argued that eliminating advanced ELA in the name of equity is regressive, limiting students' potential, and urged the board to reinstate Advanced ELA at Kennedy for all students who want the challenge.

publicComments.name: Alexis Velazquez
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade Orion student whose iReady scores indicate readiness for 8th-grade instruction asked the board to add as many advanced classes as possible at Kennedy, open to any student who feels up for the challenge.

publicComments.name: Olbia
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade Orion student planning to attend Kennedy asked the board to reinstate Advanced ELA, drawing a parallel to the existing advanced math program and arguing students with a high appetite for challenge should be grouped together.

publicComments.name: Megan
publicComments.summary: A community member supported the students' request for advanced coursework at Kennedy, arguing that limiting high achievers is ethically dubious, exacerbates achievement gaps, and that the district already has the staff and resources to expand advanced ELA across more school sites.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: Introduced herself as the new CSEA Chapter President and reported that negotiations with the district had begun productively over the past two days, thanking her team and district representatives.

publicComments.name: Diana Escalante Ocon
publicComments.summary: A librarian at Adelante Selby for 14 years, she urged the board to reconsider proposed reductions to library staff hours, explaining in detail that every minute of her 7.5-hour day is filled with essential tasks beyond checking out books.

publicComments.name: Devin Mullaney
publicComments.summary: An 8th grade teacher at Hoover expressed appreciation for the administration and support staff, specifically praised the librarians Diana and Nancy Valles, and asked the board to support them.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: A parent with four children in the Orion Mandarin Immersion Program called to express support for both MI and Co-op TK class placements at Orion, and asked the district to present accurate growth data to the community for collaborative decision-making.

publicComments.name: Carl Anders
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for HVAC upgrades and portable AC but urged the board not to use bond funds for short-term rentals, since every bond dollar costs taxpayers approximately $3.40 over 30 years, suggesting rentals be paid from the general fund and only purchases charged to the bond.

publicComments.name: Devin Mullaney
publicComments.summary: Expressed relief at the air conditioning approval but raised a concern about floor-mounted portable units taking up space in already crowded classrooms, suggesting roof-mounted permanent units would be preferable.

publicComments.summary: As a current eighth grader who has attended Connect since third grade, thanked the school for helping her learn to speak and read English and for the caring treatment by staff.

publicComments.name: Meng Zhao
publicComments.summary: Advocated for expanding the Orion Mandarin Immersion program to accommodate all interested applicants in the first round of the lottery, presenting data on growing demand, wait lists, and academic benefits of Mandarin immersion education.

publicComments.name: Michelle Strobe
publicComments.summary: Advocated for expanding the Orion Mandarin Immersion program, presenting data showing socioeconomically disadvantaged students in MI schools consistently outperform their peers, and requesting the board add an additional TK/K classroom and consider a supplemental application.

publicComments.name: Kimberly Abbey
publicComments.summary: Shared her personal experience as a TK parent in the MI program, praising its tight-knit community and the gift of Mandarin language for her son, and hoping more families can join.

publicComments.name: Weiji
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about limited kindergarten spots in the MI program as an immigrant Chinese family who moved to Redwood City specifically for the program, and asked the board to expand it.

publicComments.name: Christina Lee
publicComments.summary: Described being stuck at number one on the MI wait list for over a year while investing in private Mandarin after-school programs, and advocated for expanding the MI program so all interested families can access it.

publicComments.name: Saoirse Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade MI student shared her personal journey from struggling academically in first grade to placing 17th in a national math competition, crediting Mandarin immersion, and urged the board to support all students who need this opportunity.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Yielded time to Meng Zhao to present additional data on growth projections for Orion showing a declining trend line they believe is inaccurate, and reiterated the request to accommodate first-round applicants and consider a supplemental application.

publicComments.name: Chris Lau
publicComments.summary: Shared that he and his wife moved to Redwood City partly because of the MI program and hopes to enroll his daughter in the future, thanking the board for considering expanding it.

publicComments.name: Katherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Shared her experience as a parent whose child went through Mandarin Immersion and then Northstar, noting both programs have extensive wait lists and strong academic results, and suggested these programs merit additional resources and expanded capacity.

publicComments.name: Xingxing
publicComments.summary: Shared as a first-generation immigrant from China (with a Ukrainian immigrant husband) that they moved to Redwood City in 2019 and hope to enroll their two children in the Mandarin Immersion program for heritage language access.

publicComments.name: James Harbold
publicComments.summary: Supported the Mandarin Immersion program as a parent whose daughter is applying, noting his wife is from China and he studied Mandarin in Hong Kong, and asked the district to help families like his gain access to the program.

items.title: Adoption of Resolution No. 7, Reduction or Elimination of Certificated Services for Fiscal Year 2023-2024

publicComments.name: Esther Chan
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about reading specialist cuts and urged the district and board to find creative, sustainable long-term plans to support students.

publicComments.name: Tom Gerke
publicComments.summary: Argued that music programs are scientifically proven to benefit brain development and that Prop 28 funds should not be used as a budget safety net, urging the board not to cut arts education.

publicComments.name: Hannah Ma
publicComments.summary: Asked whether alternatives to staffing cuts were explored, raised concerns about unequal distribution of cuts across schools, and urged creative revenue generation such as facility leasing or technology donations.

publicComments.name: Lauren Abrams
publicComments.summary: Spoke as the mental health counselor at Taft, describing the high trauma levels and barriers to outside services faced by Taft students and urging reconsideration of reducing her position to 0.5 FTE.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Expressed appreciation for the district, shared data comparing Redwood City's low parcel tax to neighboring districts, and encouraged community members to support passing a larger parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Marianne Naka
publicComments.summary: Spoke as the mental health liaison at Henry Ford and urged the board to reconsider cutting mental health liaison positions at Taft, Henry Ford, Orion, and Adelante Selby.

publicComments.name: Lizbeth Estrada
publicComments.summary: Expressed deep appreciation to Dr. Baker for his focus on equity and for prioritizing the schools and students who need the most support, including special education students.

publicComments.name: Saoirse Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A fourth-grade student at Orion expressed love for her school and district, said she believes the community can adapt to budget cuts, and hoped a larger parcel tax could be passed so all kids have what they need.

publicComments.name: Sue Jorgensen
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about poor communication from the district regarding librarian layoffs, citing unprofessional disclosure of retirees' information and inadequate notice, and said she is not yet convinced to support a parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Ann Barafa
publicComments.summary: A 32-year district veteran advocated for enshrining a 25-to-1 class size ratio for K-2 classrooms in the contract, arguing that larger class sizes cause students, especially ELs and neurodivergent learners, to fall through the cracks.

publicComments.name: Sherry Tsukiyama
publicComments.summary: A first-grade teacher at Roosevelt shared personal classroom experience demonstrating that smaller class sizes (25 or fewer) allow for more individualized instruction and fewer disruptions, and urged the board to permanently cap TK-2 grades at 25 students.

publicComments.name: Jessica McLean
publicComments.summary: An education specialist described alarming projected caseload increases for special education classes and urged the board to open additional extensive support needs classrooms to reduce caseloads and ensure student safety.

publicComments.name: Allison Sudol
publicComments.summary: A first-to-third grade extensive support needs teacher described how increasing class sizes cause unsafe behaviors and dysregulation, and proposed opening one additional ESN and one SLC classroom to bring caseloads to manageable levels.

publicComments.name: Aaron Washburn
publicComments.summary: A music teacher detailed the academic, social-emotional, and cognitive benefits of music education and urged administrators and parents to advocate for a well-funded music program at every school.

publicComments.name: Diane Gutierrez
publicComments.summary: A school counselor at Orion shared a story of supporting a dysregulated student and urged the board to ensure a mental health counselor is present at every school site as an essential safety net for students.

publicComments.name: Lily Milton
publicComments.summary: An Orion and Kennedy parent and Redwood City Foundation board member urged the board to reject the resolution and pursue a more transparent, equitable, and collaborative process before cutting programs, while also supporting a parcel tax and enshrining a 25-to-1 class ratio.

publicComments.name: Dave Privasch
publicComments.summary: Acknowledged the board's difficult position but said it seems unconscionable to cut librarians, mental health staff, and STEM teachers in a high-cost area, and echoed calls for creative solutions before approving cuts.

items.title: Adoption of Resolution No. 8, Reduction of Certain Classified Services for Fiscal Year 2023-2024

publicComments.name: Salvador Gomez Nava
publicComments.summary: Spoke in Spanish (with interpretation) as a Taft parent of a seven-year-old daughter who needs counseling, urging the board to maintain school-based mental health support so children can grow up happy and succeed without the trauma going unaddressed.

publicComments.name: Ana Solorio
publicComments.summary: As CSEA Chapter 5 President, opposed the layoff of any classified employees and requested the board explore cost-cutting alternatives that do not include eliminating classified staff, asking the board not to approve the resolution.

publicComments.name: Connie Hamilton
publicComments.summary: Librarian at Clifford School questioned why three lower-paid LMA librarians are being eliminated while six new higher-paid positions may be hired, argued that her 11 years of experience is sufficient, and expressed devastation at losing her position and relationships with students.

publicComments.name: Beverly Aguilar
publicComments.summary: Librarian at Garfield School, speaking jointly with Connie Hamilton, argued that eliminating their LMA positions is unjust given their combined 30 years of experience, a pending reclassification recommendation, and the difficulty of filling six librarian vacancies, and requested the board not eliminate their positions.

publicComments.name: Ors Neighbor
publicComments.summary: Shared his son Leor's experience with dyslexia diagnosis and the financial and emotional burden of obtaining private evaluations and tutoring, urging the district to make reading support accessible regardless of family resources.

publicComments.name: Giselle Hale
publicComments.summary: As a parent of two dyslexic district students and a community advocate, she urged the board to treat dyslexia as a general education issue and highlighted districts making strides through Orton-Gillingham training for all teachers.

publicComments.name: Fallon Scoggins
publicComments.summary: Described her son Ender's severe dyslexia and dysgraphia journey, the inadequacy of pull-out-only interventions, and urged the board to make structured literacy available throughout the school day and to rethink how dyslexia is framed.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Salma
publicComments.summary: Speaking as a regional leader with Decoding Dyslexia California, she thanked the district for engaging with the California Dyslexia Guidelines and urged fidelity in program implementation and strong principal support for teachers.

publicComments.name: Ors Neighbor
publicComments.summary: Shared his son Leor's experience with dyslexia diagnosis and the financial and emotional burden of obtaining private evaluations and tutoring, urging the district to make reading support accessible regardless of family resources.

publicComments.name: Giselle Hale
publicComments.summary: As a parent of two dyslexic district students and a community advocate, she urged the board to treat dyslexia as a general education issue and highlighted districts making strides through Orton-Gillingham training for all teachers.

publicComments.name: Fallon Scoggins
publicComments.summary: Described her son Ender's severe dyslexia and dysgraphia journey, the inadequacy of pull-out-only interventions, and urged the board to make structured literacy available throughout the school day and to rethink how dyslexia is framed.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Salma
publicComments.summary: Speaking as a regional leader with Decoding Dyslexia California, she thanked the district for engaging with the California Dyslexia Guidelines and urged fidelity in program implementation and strong principal support for teachers.

Oral Communication

publicComments.name: Chris R.
publicComments.summary: Raised legal concerns about using Prop 39 bond money for workforce housing under Article 13 of the California Constitution, questioned whether teachers actually want district housing, and suggested alternative funding mechanisms such as a parcel tax or housing vouchers.

publicComments.name: Elizabeth Starks
publicComments.summary: A multilingual Redwood City resident and former ESL teacher who expressed support for retaining good teachers but emphasized the greater need for after-school spaces and resources for children left unsupervised in the community.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: As leader of the classified union chapter, she defended the equal importance of classified staff, shared her own experience of rent increases outpacing raises, and expressed strong support for workforce housing to help staff who commute long distances remain in the community.

publicComments.name: Lupe Guzmán
publicComments.summary: The principal of Hoover Community School expressed strong support for workforce housing, noting that staff who live in the community strengthen it and that housing stress causes new teachers to leave the district.

publicComments.name: Mary
publicComments.summary: A visiting San Francisco school board member asked about the quality and durability of the construction and how the rental revenues flow relative to the bond repayment.

publicComments.name: Janet Cochise
publicComments.summary: A parent in the district since 2008 described how school closures and teacher departures due to unaffordable housing have repeatedly disrupted her child's education, and raised concerns about inadequate student transportation.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: President of the Redwood City Teachers Association confirmed that teachers do want workforce housing, sharing examples of colleagues whose lives improved with affordable housing and expressing support for the plan as a way to recruit and retain quality teachers.

Welcome
Welcome by the School Board President, Cecilia Márquez
Changes to the Agenda
Additions, Deletions, or Modifications to the Agenda
Approval of Agenda
Approval of Agenda
Oral Communication

publicComments.name: Peter Cohen
publicComments.summary: Thanked district staff for correcting enrollment issues and advocated for expanding Mandarin immersion and TK programs to align with California's 2030 bilingual education goals.

publicComments.name: Alexis Betts
publicComments.summary: Asked the board to accommodate all families wanting to enroll in the Mandarin Immersion program to ensure a healthy, sustainable program through eighth grade.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly
publicComments.summary: Advocated for underserved families in the MI program, requested a different school structure to better serve both programs, and urged the district to apply for the TCLP program for additional teacher support.

publicComments.name: William Dennis
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for sibling priority in the Mandarin Immersion program so his younger daughter could attend the same school as his son.

publicComments.name: Deepika Germany (speaker was husband)
publicComments.summary: Advocated for an additional TK class in the Mandarin Immersion program, noting his daughter is currently on the waitlist.

publicComments.name: Tina Chung
publicComments.summary: Advocated for additional Mandarin Immersion TK classes to benefit more students, including her son who knows some Mandarin.

publicComments.name: Ronnie Le
publicComments.summary: Advocated for continuing and expanding the Mandarin Immersion program, citing high academic performance data and the importance of bilingual education for her incoming kindergartener.

publicComments.name: Jackie Chen
publicComments.summary: Described the stressful waitlist experience for the MI program and requested two TK MI classes and three kindergarten MI classes.

publicComments.name: Julia Selesneva
publicComments.summary: Praised the academic rigor of the Mandarin Immersion program and advocated for expanding kindergarten and TK enrollment.

publicComments.name: Alex (last name not given)
publicComments.summary: Supported expansion of the Mandarin Immersion TK and kindergarten programs, connecting early bilingual immersion to values like open-mindedness and empathy.

publicComments.name: Angela Kang
publicComments.summary: Advocated for additional MI TK classes so that all interested families, including hers, could have the opportunity to enroll their children.

publicComments.name: Sam Christensen
publicComments.summary: Stated that the Mandarin Immersion program is the only school option his family is interested in and expressed support for expanding the TK program.

publicComments.name: Chris Terry
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about fairness in the MI lottery, specifically the Odyssey Preschool preference and TK sibling preference crowding out other kindergarten applicants, and asked the board to reform the lottery or add more classes.

publicComments.name: Jasper Chen
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for building a great community and encouraged investment in and expansion of the Mandarin Immersion program.

publicComments.name: Anna Lee Moraz
publicComments.summary: A Spanish-speaking parent from Mexico raised concerns about accessibility of the MI program for low-income families, including the cost of after-school programs.

publicComments.name: Keith Simmons
publicComments.summary: Requested expansion of sibling priority to TK, two TK MI classes, three kindergarten MI classes, and urged the board to examine the Adelante program's waitlist given the importance of early language acquisition.

publicComments.name: Heather Stamper
publicComments.summary: Supported expanding TK and kindergarten MI classes to stabilize enrollment and prevent attrition that weakens the program in upper grades.

publicComments.name: Mele Rosallo
publicComments.summary: Advocated for more funding and support resources for MI students with learning disabilities, including a Mandarin resource teacher and additional TK access.

publicComments.name: Richard Pont
publicComments.summary: Shared his family's positive experience with the MI program and requested expansion so other families with children, including those with IEPs, can participate.

publicComments.name: Micah Bonara
publicComments.summary: Shared relief that his twin boys got off the MI waitlist and supported expansion of the TK and kindergarten MI programs to spare families the emotional stress of the waitlist process.

publicComments.name: Sarah Rutherford
publicComments.summary: Asked for consistency in the sibling priority policy between TK and other grades, especially in light of Universal TK expansion.

publicComments.name: Tiffany Chao Bev
publicComments.summary: Stated that the Mandarin Immersion program was a reason her family moved to Redwood City and urged expansion of TK and kindergarten MI classes.

publicComments.name: Xiang Yen
publicComments.summary: Asked how the community could help move forward MI program expansion, offering to write letters or take other actions as guided by the board.

publicComments.name: Julia Feng
publicComments.summary: Questioned whether the district should artificially cap demand for the MI program and emphasized the narrow TK/kindergarten enrollment window for immersion learners.

publicComments.name: Doshi (first name not given)
publicComments.summary: Advocated for adding an MI TK class, noting her daughter is on the waitlist and that out-of-district families are also seeking to enroll, making competition even harder for in-district residents.

publicComments.name: Philip Guy
publicComments.summary: Thanked the district for the MI program and asked the board to expand it as much as possible, offering community support to help make that happen.

publicComments.name: Olanes Villanueva (interpreted)
publicComments.summary: A Spanish-speaking parent with three children in the MI program asked for more support for Latino families in the program, including in-school tutoring services so children are not left behind.

publicComments.name: Ileana Harrison
publicComments.summary: Thanked Dr. Baker for recognizing MI performers at the Lunar New Year fair and requested two TK MI classes and three kindergarten MI classes.

publicComments.name: Kyle Zipes
publicComments.summary: Argued that a lottery for school placement is unacceptable and urged the board to accommodate all MI-interested families, suggesting a dedicated campus if needed.

publicComments.name: Dennis McBride
publicComments.summary: Paid tribute to María Díaz-Slocum's 21 years of service, highlighting her dedication to students, her calm leadership, and her role as the face of the school board on the Bayside.

publicComments.name: Ninfa and Secundino (Familia Unidas representatives)
publicComments.summary: On behalf of Familia Unidas parents and students, thanked María for her incredible support in helping hundreds of families achieve success through literacy and learning.

publicComments.name: Giselle Hill
publicComments.summary: As a freshly retired city official, praised María as a giant in Redwood City whose work on equity predated broad discussions of equity, and welcomed new trustee David Weekley and congratulated Cecilia Márquez.

publicComments.name: Michelle Torres
publicComments.summary: Thanked María and Familia Unidas for unconditional support, sharing how the program helped her feel at home, supported her family's educational goals, and led to her son's improved academic performance.

publicComments.name: Beatriz Fernanda Senda
publicComments.summary: An 11-year-old Familia Unidas member since preschool shared how the program taught her about reading, math, technology, health, and science, and expressed hope that the program continues.

publicComments.name: Laura Ramirez
publicComments.summary: Thanked María and Familia Unidas for helping her navigate the educational system in a new country and for instilling reading and healthy habits that benefited her son's schooling.

publicComments.name: Chris Robel
publicComments.summary: Opposed the bond measure, arguing a parcel tax would be more equitable, that bond financing benefits investors at taxpayers' expense, and that declining enrollment and poor academic outcomes call into question whether facilities investment is the right priority.

publicComments.name: Katerina Schwaidenbeck
publicComments.summary: Supported the bond, citing broken bathrooms and the lack of a central kitchen as facility problems that directly affect student health and learning.

publicComments.name: Jessica Shade
publicComments.summary: Supported the bond, highlighting the need to meet health and safety standards, potential for a central kitchen, community benefits of improved schools, and the district's track record of completing Measure T on time and under budget.

publicComments.name: Jessica Meunier
publicComments.summary: Supported the bond, expressing enthusiasm for the central kitchen component to improve meal quality and for updated safety standards, noting confidence based on the prior bond's on-time, under-budget delivery.

publicComments.name: Elmer Martinez
publicComments.summary: Supported the bond as a community volunteer and former Roosevelt student, emphasizing the need for critical facility upgrades at aging schools to ensure safe, quality learning environments and strong community and property values.

publicComments.name: Ileana Harrison
publicComments.summary: Supported the bond as a pediatrician and parent of incoming students at Orion Alternative School, praising the new building from Measure T, reporting broad parent support, and strongly endorsing the central kitchen component to enable cooking fresh, healthy meals for students.

publicComments.name: Matt Schwal
publicComments.summary: Argued the NSA Forward Committee was negatively framed and called on board members to reframe the discussion positively and inspire change rather than break what is working.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals are rushed and lack an evidence-based approach, and proposed a 'SHINE' talent development program modeled on the U46 district's AIM program to serve all neighborhood school students rather than restructuring North Star.

publicComments.name: Tony Webel
publicComments.summary: Shared his experience as both a Roosevelt and North Star parent, argued there is no data justifying grade configuration or location changes, and cited board bylaws requiring decisions be based on student learning and achievement.

publicComments.name: Diana Fu
publicComments.summary: Drew on her experience helping start the MI program to argue the district should provide more and better school choices rather than taking away the North Star option from parents.

publicComments.name: Lone Hin
publicComments.summary: Described her son's unmet needs at his neighborhood school and argued that dismantling or scaling back North Star would not serve any children in the district.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Neill
publicComments.summary: Argued that options A through C would eliminate half of North Star and fail to meet the stated goal of serving more students more effectively, and that no changes should happen until neighborhood schools can serve the needs of academically challenged students.

publicComments.name: Matt Collier
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to choose an option that allows K–8 programming to continue as a standalone school, sharing his personal experience benefiting from similar magnet programs.

publicComments.name: Anthony Low
publicComments.summary: As a Roy Cloud and North Star parent, argued all four options are deficient, that three of them effectively close 50% of North Star, and that his family would likely have to leave the district if a 6–8 option were chosen.

publicComments.name: Andrew Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Argued the board should focus on lifting lower-performing parts of the district rather than negatively impacting the award-winning North Star, and urged the board not to hastily approve incomplete recommendations.

publicComments.name: Heidi Wall
publicComments.summary: Argued the district should focus on systemic problems rather than dismantling a successful school, and cited the U46 model as a proven approach to improving diversity without restructuring.

publicComments.name: Susan Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Opposed the quota cap on neighborhood school transfers to NSA, arguing it would increase perceptions of elitism and division, and asked why the cap is not applied to all school-of-choice programs.

publicComments.name: Costas Dimitropoulos
publicComments.summary: Called for empirical evidence and proven models to justify any changes to North Star, noting that demographic differences between schools reflect local demographics rather than the influence of North Star.

publicComments.name: Kelly McCarthy
publicComments.summary: Questioned why the district is prioritizing North Star changes when so many students are underperforming post-COVID, and urged the board to use those resources to bolster neighborhood school programs instead.

publicComments.name: Casey Wright
publicComments.summary: Called the four options deeply flawed and irresponsible without fuller analysis of consequences, urged the board to postpone consideration and demand new options like those proposed by Cameron Hoffman.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Noted that all speakers before her opposed changes to North Star, and argued that the 'rising tide lifts all boats' principle means the school should be kept as-is rather than changed to reduce resentment from other schools.

publicComments.name: Gautam Dutta
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent and community leader, echoed the sentiment that North Star is working well for his daughter and urged the board to reject all four options and instead focus on improving access and resources for all schools.

publicComments.name: Jing Su
publicComments.summary: Warned that the proposed changes would create many unhappy parents who would become reliable voters opposing the board, and urged trustees to consider the daily disruption to North Star families before making their decision.

publicComments.name: Kirsten McMullen
publicComments.summary: Argued the recommendations lack an evidence-based approach, only adequately solve the third-grade attrition problem while creating new unknowns, and urged additional research before selecting any option.

publicComments.name: Bara Altaba
publicComments.summary: As a parent of current NSA students who came from private school because of NSA, urged the board not to break a nationally recognized school and instead look at how to bring other schools up to NSA's level.

publicComments.name: Michelle Fogarty
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals take direct aim at one successful school rather than addressing full district needs, and urged the board to take more time, examine the data framework, and conduct a new community survey before acting.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member, encouraged the board to move forward with the 6–8 Bayside option as the one proposal that addresses all three charges given to the committee.

publicComments.name: Christopher Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to reject all four proposals and pause major changes, arguing the NSA Forward process was flawed from the beginning due to outdated and biased data, and called for a new community pulse survey.

publicComments.name: David Wright
publicComments.summary: Implored the board to defer the decision and request revised options informed by data that directly align to the committee's stated goals, rather than committing to deeply flawed options.

publicComments.name: Mike Beebe
publicComments.summary: Identified three broadly supported elements from Dr. Baker's plans (publicizing NSA, test prep/logistics help, and transportation), suggested spreading entrance grades across 3rd–5th to blunt the third-grade attrition pinch, and argued the board's primary focus should be the 52–72% of district students not at grade level.

publicComments.name: Meredith Park
publicComments.summary: As a Sequoia High parent and safe-routes advocate, warned that adding K–2 at the Duane location would worsen traffic, and suggested considering a neighborhood boundary middle school with an IB program at that site instead.

publicComments.name: Nathan Schmidt
publicComments.summary: Used a boat analogy to argue the board must focus on lifting underperforming schools rather than 'dumping water' into the one that is floating, urging them not to take action merely to appear as change agents.

publicComments.name: Mohamed Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: Ceded his time to Cameron Hoffman, agreed with her sentiments, and called the entire process a waste of resources that should have gone toward educating lower-income students, urging trustees to reject all options.

publicComments.name: Lily Melton
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent, urged the board to move forward with bold structural changes, noting that a large community of district parents supports significant changes even if they are not the loudest voices tonight.

publicComments.name: Beatrice Chan
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent, asked the board to present new options focused on introducing enrichment programs at community schools and helping current students meet grade-level expectations, rather than dismantling a successful model.

publicComments.name: Maribel Ng
publicComments.summary: Shared her daughter's struggles before finding North Star and argued that spreading the North Star philosophy of seeing students as individuals and loving what you teach across all Redwood City schools would fix many district-wide problems.

publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals are rushed and lack an evidence-based approach, and proposed a 'SHINE' talent development program modeled on the U46 district's AIM program to serve all neighborhood school students rather than restructuring North Star.

publicComments.name: Tony Webel
publicComments.summary: Shared his experience as both a Roosevelt and North Star parent, argued there is no data justifying grade configuration or location changes, and cited board bylaws requiring decisions be based on student learning and achievement.

publicComments.name: Diana Fu
publicComments.summary: Drew on her experience helping start the MI program to argue the district should provide more and better school choices rather than taking away the North Star option from parents.

publicComments.name: Lone Hin
publicComments.summary: Described her son's unmet needs at his neighborhood school and argued that dismantling or scaling back North Star would not serve any children in the district.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Neill
publicComments.summary: Argued that options A through C would eliminate half of North Star and fail to meet the stated goal of serving more students more effectively, and that no changes should happen until neighborhood schools can serve the needs of academically challenged students.

publicComments.name: Matt Collier
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to choose an option that allows K–8 programming to continue as a standalone school, sharing his personal experience benefiting from similar magnet programs.

publicComments.name: Anthony Low
publicComments.summary: As a Roy Cloud and North Star parent, argued all four options are deficient, that three of them effectively close 50% of North Star, and that his family would likely have to leave the district if a 6–8 option were chosen.

publicComments.name: Andrew Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Argued the board should focus on lifting lower-performing parts of the district rather than negatively impacting the award-winning North Star, and urged the board not to hastily approve incomplete recommendations.

publicComments.name: Heidi Wall
publicComments.summary: Argued the district should focus on systemic problems rather than dismantling a successful school, and cited the U46 model as a proven approach to improving diversity without restructuring.

publicComments.name: Susan Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Opposed the quota cap on neighborhood school transfers to NSA, arguing it would increase perceptions of elitism and division, and asked why the cap is not applied to all school-of-choice programs.

publicComments.name: Costas Dimitropoulos
publicComments.summary: Called for empirical evidence and proven models to justify any changes to North Star, noting that demographic differences between schools reflect local demographics rather than the influence of North Star.

publicComments.name: Kelly McCarthy
publicComments.summary: Questioned why the district is prioritizing North Star changes when so many students are underperforming post-COVID, and urged the board to use those resources to bolster neighborhood school programs instead.

publicComments.name: Casey Wright
publicComments.summary: Called the four options deeply flawed and irresponsible without fuller analysis of consequences, urged the board to postpone consideration and demand new options like those proposed by Cameron Hoffman.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Noted that all speakers before her opposed changes to North Star, and argued that the 'rising tide lifts all boats' principle means the school should be kept as-is rather than changed to reduce resentment from other schools.

publicComments.name: Gautam Dutta
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent and community leader, echoed the sentiment that North Star is working well for his daughter and urged the board to reject all four options and instead focus on improving access and resources for all schools.

publicComments.name: Jing Su
publicComments.summary: Warned that the proposed changes would create many unhappy parents who would become reliable voters opposing the board, and urged trustees to consider the daily disruption to North Star families before making their decision.

publicComments.name: Kirsten McMullen
publicComments.summary: Argued the recommendations lack an evidence-based approach, only adequately solve the third-grade attrition problem while creating new unknowns, and urged additional research before selecting any option.

publicComments.name: Bara Altaba
publicComments.summary: As a parent of current NSA students who came from private school because of NSA, urged the board not to break a nationally recognized school and instead look at how to bring other schools up to NSA's level.

publicComments.name: Michelle Fogarty
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals take direct aim at one successful school rather than addressing full district needs, and urged the board to take more time, examine the data framework, and conduct a new community survey before acting.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member, encouraged the board to move forward with the 6–8 Bayside option as the one proposal that addresses all three charges given to the committee.

publicComments.name: Christopher Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to reject all four proposals and pause major changes, arguing the NSA Forward process was flawed from the beginning due to outdated and biased data, and called for a new community pulse survey.

publicComments.name: David Wright
publicComments.summary: Implored the board to defer the decision and request revised options informed by data that directly align to the committee's stated goals, rather than committing to deeply flawed options.

publicComments.name: Mike Beebe
publicComments.summary: Identified three broadly supported elements from Dr. Baker's plans (publicizing NSA, test prep/logistics help, and transportation), suggested spreading entrance grades across 3rd–5th to blunt the third-grade attrition pinch, and argued the board's primary focus should be the 52–72% of district students not at grade level.

publicComments.name: Meredith Park
publicComments.summary: As a Sequoia High parent and safe-routes advocate, warned that adding K–2 at the Duane location would worsen traffic, and suggested considering a neighborhood boundary middle school with an IB program at that site instead.

publicComments.name: Nathan Schmidt
publicComments.summary: Used a boat analogy to argue the board must focus on lifting underperforming schools rather than 'dumping water' into the one that is floating, urging them not to take action merely to appear as change agents.

publicComments.name: Mohamed Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: Ceded his time to Cameron Hoffman, agreed with her sentiments, and called the entire process a waste of resources that should have gone toward educating lower-income students, urging trustees to reject all options.

publicComments.name: Lily Melton
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent, urged the board to move forward with bold structural changes, noting that a large community of district parents supports significant changes even if they are not the loudest voices tonight.

publicComments.name: Beatrice Chan
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent, asked the board to present new options focused on introducing enrichment programs at community schools and helping current students meet grade-level expectations, rather than dismantling a successful model.

publicComments.name: Maribel Ng
publicComments.summary: Shared her daughter's struggles before finding North Star and argued that spreading the North Star philosophy of seeing students as individuals and loving what you teach across all Redwood City schools would fix many district-wide problems.

Discussion Items

publicComments.name: David Weekley
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to keep students at the center of this process, ensuring North Star changes if it harms any students and that the focus remains on maximizing the potential of every student in the district.

publicComments.name: Lily Milton
publicComments.summary: Speaking as a North Star Forward Committee member and Orion parent, she expressed appreciation for the process and presented the subcommittee's key recommendations: changing grade configuration so North Star no longer begins at third grade, and bringing compacted curriculum and enrichment to all schools, while urging the board to act with urgency on broader equity issues.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker
publicComments.summary: Argued that the Bayside access data is misleading since many Bayside families already access North Star via school of choice, that North Star is not broken and serves its community at no extra cost, and urged the board to focus on the 70% of students who are academically behind rather than restructuring a well-designed school.

publicComments.name: John Kinsel
publicComments.summary: Expressed strong support for North Star as a program that keeps academically advanced students engaged and challenged, and suggested the real focus should be on improving conditions at other schools rather than changing North Star.

publicComments.name: Owen Webel
publicComments.summary: As a North Star graduate, shared that his previous school left him disengaged due to lack of challenge, while North Star allowed him to make friends at his own level and progress further academically.

publicComments.name: Tony Webel
publicComments.summary: As a North Star committee member and parent of children at both Roosevelt and North Star, he emphasized that the primary objective should be the best equitable learning environment for all students, and raised concerns that some committee ideas conflict with that goal, also requesting the Jamboard document be removed from materials as rushed and misleading.

publicComments.name: Jessica Nodi
publicComments.summary: As a Roy Cloud parent and educator, expressed support for starting North Star at kindergarten, bringing the enrichment model to all students at all sites, and offering equal enrollment percentages from all schools.

publicComments.name: Katie Morello
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent, described the emotional impact on her daughter losing 15 classmates and suggested that if North Star is a strong accelerated school, middle school might be a more appropriate entry point.

publicComments.name: Kaylee Vega
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent who chose the district partly because of North Star, argued that North Star is not the problem and that the other district schools being under-resourced and underperforming is the real issue, urging the board not to dismantle a highly ranked program.

publicComments.name: Loan Hin
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent who personally benefited from a magnet school as a child, stated her family would leave the district if North Star is not available at third grade, and argued that equity and access issues can be addressed without eliminating the North Star format.

publicComments.name: Elle Kolekar
publicComments.summary: As a Bayside family with children attending Hillside schools including North Star, argued that the equity problem is a deeper district-wide issue not caused solely by North Star, and called on the board to invest in and strengthen Bayside community schools.

publicComments.name: Alice Harkey
publicComments.summary: As North Star's parent club president, described the transformational impact of North Star on her children, expressed support for universal testing and expanded outreach including busing and after-school support for Bayside students, and asked the board to preserve North Star's curriculum and enrichment opportunities.

publicComments.name: Shonda Stewart
publicComments.summary: As a parent with children at both North Star and Orion, argued that North Star's parent fundraising perpetuates educational inequality, that the school culture is not socioeconomically inclusive, and that outreach to Bayside schools has been inadequate compared to Mandarin immersion community outreach.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member focused on third grade attrition, argued that enriched programming should be available to all RCSD students regardless of testing, since no student is more in need of enrichment than any other, and urged the board to pursue equity and justice for all students.

publicComments.name: Nicole Kowaki
publicComments.summary: Reading a condensed letter co-signed by 20 district parents, cited stark demographic disparities between North Star and the broader district to argue that North Star as currently constituted amounts to publicly funded education for the affluent, and urged the board to support the equitable solutions proposed by the North Star Forward Committee.

publicComments.name: Daryl Norcott
publicComments.summary: As a Clifford parent, argued that North Star inherently widens the achievement gap, that standardized testing is racially biased, that children who don't get in feel stigmatized, and that the enrichment model should be brought to students at their neighborhood schools rather than concentrating resources at one location.

publicComments.name: Heidi von Brielle
publicComments.summary: Raised environmental concerns about the carbon footprint of families driving to North Star, argued that the culture of school transfers undermines neighborhood school funding and volunteerism, and urged the board to implement options that would end the 'musical chairs' dynamic, including possibly a Bayside hub.

publicComments.name: Mike Beebe
publicComments.summary: As a North Star third-grade parent who also has children in the district, urged the board to carefully examine whether the issue is one of admissions process or information and logistics, cautioning against a hard percent-admit model before exhausting outreach and transportation solutions.

publicComments.name: Ann Hinesek
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member, highlighted bringing the Renzulli method to all schools and equalizing PTO fundraising distribution as key equity recommendations, and expressed personal support for changing the grade configuration, adding Spanish-speaking staff, capping school admittance, and possibly moving North Star to the Bayside.

items.title: Second Reading and Approval of Board Policy 5116.1 - Intradistrict Open Enrollment

publicComments.name: David Weekley
publicComments.summary: Opposed the proposed transfer restriction, arguing it harms students and the district by reducing choice and will ultimately hurt enrollment in programs like Mandarin Immersion.

publicComments.name: Eric Liu
publicComments.summary: Opposed the policy as a Chinese-American parent of a Mandarin Immersion student, saying the proposal felt discriminatory by barring MI families from competing for North Star.

publicComments.name: Connie Kwan
publicComments.summary: Raised the unintended consequence that parents might be forced to pull their child from MI and place them in private school for a year just to preserve the option to apply to North Star.

publicComments.name: Peter Kwan
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about timing, the fundamental problem of attrition rather than the symptom, and the lack of transparency around 'unspoken rules' in choice program enrollment.

publicComments.name: Dennis Lee
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a rising kindergartner newly accepted to MI, he opposed the policy for forcing families to predict years ahead what is best for their child and for penalizing choice-school families while potentially benefiting private school families.

publicComments.name: Michelle Hsu
publicComments.summary: Argued the root issue is that North Star and Mandarin Immersion are not set up on fair ground due to North Star's third-grade start and admissions process, and urged the committee to address equity in North Star admissions.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Barnett
publicComments.summary: Called the policy shortsighted and harmful to enrollment, arguing it will increase inequity, may turn North Star into a publicly funded private school, and urged addressing North Star's own issues instead.

publicComments.name: Diana Chang
publicComments.summary: Submitted written comment opposing the restriction as unnecessarily limiting for families who discover their first choice school is not the right fit, and asked the board to find more rational ways to achieve their objectives.

publicComments.name: Alvin Cheon
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent participation parent, expressed concern that removing the North Star incentive would push committed families out of RCSD, and suggested alternatives such as distributing North Star-style culture across schools rather than concentrating it at one site.

publicComments.name: Christina Jade Lee Simmons
publicComments.summary: Urged the district to address structural inequality perpetuated by the North Star model, suggested starting North Star at sixth grade, and called for more enrichment across all elementary schools.

publicComments.name: Kyle Zeibes
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for postponing the policy, argued it would harm equity and push families to private school, and suggested delaying North Star to sixth grade as a cleaner solution.

publicComments.name: Brian Hicks
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposed policy is the opposite of any long-standing unwritten rule, urged addressing the real problem rather than restricting choice, and requested that any new policy not apply retroactively to families already enrolled.

publicComments.name: Elle Kolekar
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent participation parent with a child starting there in the fall, warned that the policy would drive families to private school and could effectively end the parent participation program.

publicComments.name: Keith Simmons
publicComments.summary: Echoed earlier concerns and highlighted that the superintendent-exception carve-out could create racial inequities because language and cultural barriers make it harder for immigrant families to petition for exceptions.

publicComments.name: Ting Cheng Wang
publicComments.summary: Opposed the policy because it effectively forces parents of kindergartners to choose their child's middle school years in advance, which is unfair.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: As Orion PTO co-president, argued that the fundamental problem is North Star's structure and its perceived status as the 'best' school, and that the policy would not ultimately harm MI recruitment since committed immersion families exist and the program has a waitlist.

publicComments.name: Elizabeth Flavel
publicComments.summary: Shared her experience choosing Adelante partly because she knew she could leave if it didn't work out, and cautioned that the policy may have unintended consequences for incoming families' enrollment decisions.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Praised board members who spoke in favor of reopening, urged the administration to adopt a more decisive and urgent tone, and noted that by the county's own definition only Taft School has formally reopened, calling on the district to commit to reopening all schools by the return from spring break.

publicComments.name: Allison Oford
publicComments.summary: Requested the district publish a regular reopening dashboard for transparency, thanked staff working in person, and argued that returning students to campus this school year is worthwhile for mental health, screen-time reduction, and preparing for a stronger fall return.

publicComments.name: Mary Beth Maloney
publicComments.summary: Welcomed the board's progress toward reopening but stressed the need for a concrete plan for middle school students to return to campus, urging the district to think creatively and not leave tweens and teens behind.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Kwiajkowski
publicComments.summary: As a child and adolescent psychiatrist, described worsening mental health impacts of distance learning on children and implored the board to reopen schools immediately, citing national expert guidance, low county transmission rates, and firsthand evidence of rapid student improvement upon returning to campus.

publicComments.name: Katherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Stated she would not send her child back to school until a COVID vaccine is available for children and argued that distance learning options, including Mandarin immersion, should continue for families who are not ready to return.

publicComments.name: Heidi
publicComments.summary: Expressed that the board's prior lack of guidance has created mistrust between teachers and parents, called on the board to be more proactive and decisive, highlighted concerns about children being left behind in distance learning, and applauded the forward progress made at this meeting.
